findings.description: Port 22 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on a publicly addressable instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploitation of the SSH service.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and no TLS listener is configured, so all portal traffic traverses the internet in cleartext.
Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unconstrained outbound channel for data exfiltration or command-and-control from a compromised instance.

User data exports a static AWS access key ID and secret access key. EC2 user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by any process or SSRF vector on the host, leaking long-lived IAM credentials.
No metadata_options block sets http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled and the credentials/user-data in metadata can be read through a simple SSRF in the public-facing Apache service.
The instance does not specify root_block_device with encrypted = true, so the root EBS volume may be stored unencrypted at rest.
The instance is launched in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and routed to an internet gateway, placing it directly on the internet with no load balancer, bastion, or NAT boundary.
The EBS data volume attached to the portal server does not set encrypted = true, leaving stored data unencrypted at rest and in snapshots.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted EBS volume, so the backup copy of the data is also stored without encryption.
The VPC flow log archive bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so sensitive network telemetry is stored unencrypted.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ACL, or bucket policy is defined for the flow log bucket, so it is not protected against accidental public ACL or policy grants.
No bucket policy enforces aws:SecureTransport, permitting flow log objects to be read or written over unencrypted HTTP.

findings.issue_category: force destroy enabled on log store
findings.description: force_destroy = true allows the audit/flow-log bucket and all of its objects to be deleted without emptying it first, undermining the integrity and availability of security evidence.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP, removing the network boundary by default.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP, removing the network boundary by default.
